chunks: Muhammad ibn Ismail narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Rib'i, from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Al-Fudayl said to him (peace be upon him): 'Do you marry the Nasibi (Hostile one)?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, and there is no prestige.' I said: 'May I be sacrificed for you! By Allah, I am only saying this to you, and even if she came to me with a house filled with dirhams, I would not do it.'

key_terms.النَّاصِبَة: Nasibi: A female who is hostile to the Ahl al-Bayt, often used to describe those who opposed Ali ibn Abi Talib.
key_terms.جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ: Ju'iltu fidaka: May I be sacrificed for you; a common phrase of respect and devotion used by companions when addressing the Imams.
key_terms.لَا كَرَامَة: La karamah: No prestige or honor; indicating that the marriage lacks spiritual or social value.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on marrying a Nasibi woman in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes the prohibition of marrying a 'Nasibi' (one hostile to the Ahl al-Bayt), a ruling confirmed by al-Fudayl ibn Yasar’s emphatic refusal of immense wealth to illustrate that spiritual fidelity outweighs material gain. This hadith, found in *Al-Kafi*, underscores the significance of *al-wala'* and *al-bara'* (affinity and enmity) in marital compatibility within Shia jurisprudence. The narrative highlights that hostility to the Imams constitutes a fundamental defect in religious standing, making such marriages spiritually detrimental.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin ShAzaan, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Rabie, from Al Fuzayl Bin Yasaar, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws, said, ‘

Fuzayl said to himasws, ‘Can I marry the Hostile woman (Nasibi)?’ Heasws said: ‘No, and there is no prestige’. I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for youasws! By Allahazwj, I am only saying this to youasws, and even if she comes to me with a house filled with Dirhams, I would not do it’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn ‘Isma’il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Rib’iy from Fudayl ibn Yasar who has said the following: “This is concerning my question before abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, if I can marry al-Nasibah (one hostile to ‘A’immah).

He (the Imam) said, ‘No, it is not an honor.’ I then said, ‘I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause, I just say it but even if she comes to me with a whole house full of dirham I will not do so.’”
